video.description:
Learn to explain how to run async work in parallel safely: Async Let, Task Group & Structured Concurrency, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Async Let - A way to start a child task now and read its result later with `await`.
Task Group - A group of child tasks that run together while you collect each result.
Structured Concurrency - A style where child tasks live inside their parent, so the parent finishes only after they do.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Async Let - A way to start a child task now and read its result later with `await`.
한국어: Async Let: 자식 태스크를 지금 시작하고 결과는 나중에 await로 읽는 방법

Task Group - A group of child tasks that run together while you collect each result.

Structured Concurrency - A style where child tasks live inside their parent, so the parent finishes only after they do.
한국어: Structured Concurrency: 자식 태스크가 부모 안에 머물러 부모가 자식이 끝난 뒤에만 끝나는 방식

landscape.hook: Can you explain Async Let, Task Group and Structured Concurrency in English?

dialogue.title: Load it all at once
dialogue.setting: A screen that loads data too slowly

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my screen loads the user and the posts one after another, and it feels slow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use async let. It starts a child task now, and you read the result later with await.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Both start right away, and they run at the same time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if I have twenty images, not just two?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then use a task group. A task group lets you add child tasks in a loop and collect each result.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do I need to stop the child tasks myself if the screen closes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. That is structured concurrency. The child tasks live inside their parent.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the parent waits for them?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, the parent finishes only after the children do. That is the rule of structured concurrency.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That sounds safe. I will try async let first.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. And use a task group when the number of tasks changes.
Use async let to start both requests.
